title: Sherlock Holmes: A Study in Scarlet — Ep 03/14 — "The Lauriston Garden Mystery"
description:
A Study in Scarlet, Episode 3. A note comes to Baker Street, and Watson follows Holmes to an empty house off the Brixton Road where a well-dressed man lies dead on the floor.

Told in Watson's own voice, cut to under three minutes. Holmes will not hurry inside. He walks the pavement, stares at the mud, stops twice and smiles once, and Watson cannot see what there is to smile at. The room is bare but for the body: well fed, clean shaven, a card in his pocket giving the name Enoch J. Drebber of Cleveland, Ohio. There is blood in that room and no wound anywhere upon him. Then a match is struck in the darkest corner, and one word stands on the bare plaster in letters of blood.

SOURCE
"A Study in Scarlet" by Arthur Conan Doyle, first published 1887. This episode adapts Chapter III, "The Lauriston Garden Mystery". The book is in the public domain. Full text from Project Gutenberg: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/244

HOW THIS WAS MADE
Every picture and every voice in this video is generated with AI. The words are adapted from Arthur Conan Doyle's text and edited by a person; the narration is a synthetic voice, not a recording of anyone; no shot is footage of a real person, a real place or a real event. This video is also declared as altered or synthetic content in YouTube's own disclosure field.

THE SERIES
Fourteen chapters, fourteen episodes, in order.
